summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Pelican Cloud. High-level alignment on integration patterns: marketplace integration, optional private deployment (VPC/on-prem), and a 4-6 week pilot focused on a model serving proof point. Customer cares about compliance, predictable throughput, and minimal infra changes. Agreed to share materials and schedule technical deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do quick intros then dive into what you're hoping to explore with Redwood.
[00:00:12] Rina (Pelican): Thanks, Lena. Hi all, I'm Rina, head of partnerships at Pelican. We run a marketplace for AI workloads and we're exploring onramps for managed inference providers.
[00:00:28] Marcus (Redwood SE): Hey Rina, Devon, Anika — Marcus here, I'm the SE, I'll focus on the technical fit. Quick note, sorry if the audio is a bit wobbly on my side.
[00:00:36] Devon (Pelican): No worries.
[00:00:40] Lena: Quick agenda: 1) understand Pelican marketplace constraints, 2) integration models (hosted API vs private/VPC), 3) compliance questions, 4) propose next steps. Sound OK?
[00:00:50] Rina: Yep. We'll also want to discuss commercial + go-to-market aspects but this call is mostly technical discovery.
[00:00:58] Marcus: Great. Devon, maybe can you give a quick picture of your infra? GPUs, clusters, whether you prefer an SDK integration or direct API calls for marketplace partners?
[00:01:10] Devon: Sure. We're on a mixed cloud footprint — mostly our own tenancy on CloudGiant but also on customer-prem for certain regulated customers. For GPU fleets we run A100 and some older V100s, k8s clusters managed via kube-proxy (they said kubernetis earlier). The marketplace runs as a multi-tenant layer on top. Ideally we'd let partners offer hosted endpoints but we need strong tenancy and audit logs.
[00:01:40] Marcus: OK, that tracks. On the Redwood side we have three main modes: hosted API, Reserved/Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For marketplace plug-ins people usually start with hosted for speed, then move to dedicated or private for regulated customers.
[00:01:58] Rina: Can you explain the dedicated option? We had a call with FalconServe and they said dedicated means we lease a pool of GPUs — is it similar?
[00:02:08] Lena: Yes, similar concept. Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with SLA targets and predictable throughput. You can pin model versions, configure autoscale, and set routing policies. We call out predictable latency SLOs and fallbacks to cheaper variants if capacity spikes.
[00:02:26] Rina: Nice. 
[00:02:28] Devon: A few constraints — our marketplace requires per-tenant audit trails, SSO/SCIM for partner onboarding, and customer data residency controls. Also some partners can't leave their model weights off-prem.
[00:02:42] Marcus: We have KMS/HSM integrations for key management and audit logs exposed via our console. For on-prem weight constraints we do a Private deployment — a customer-managed control plane with optional on-prem runtime, or VPC peering. Sometimes the transcription engine munges 'KV cache' as 'KV cash' but we do key-value cache management in the runtime too.
[00:03:04] Anika (Pelican): If we did a private deploy, how much infra change is needed from our side? Our marketplace runs in its own VPC and we try to avoid touching partner infra setups.
[00:03:14] Marcus: Usually customers either bring a small agent and accept traffic via VPC peering, or we install the runtime into a managed namespace. For the former there's minimal change — we ask for a service subnet, egress rules, and an internal load balancer. If you want fully air-gapped, that's more ops but we support it.
[00:03:33] Devon: What about autoscaling? Marketplace demand is spiky.
[00:03:37] Lena: Our Dedicated product supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. Also we have smart routing so low-priority requests can be routed to cheaper variants or queued.
[00:03:47] Rina: Latency vs cost — common tradeoff. Do you have quantization options to reduce cost?
[00:03:53] Marcus: Yes we recommend quantized model variants for cost-sensitive paths. Our runtime supports optimized kernels for quantized ops; the SE team can produce a quantize recommendation per model. There's also prefix caching / KV cache to reduce per-token compute for repeated prompts. (transcription often shows 'KV cash' here).
[00:04:14] Mateo (Pelican Security): On compliance: SOC2 and ISO are core. We need to know your retention defaults and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM. Also what SSO protocols you support.
[00:04:25] Lena: We are SOC2 Type II and provide audit logs, SAML/SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and KMS integrations. We'll send the security one-pager.
[00:04:35] Devon: Good. For a pilot, we'll want a test harness — can you do a perf run against our representative workload? We'll need to measure 95th percentile latency at production-ish load and token throughput.
[00:04:45] Marcus: Absolutely. For the pilot we usually set up a small dedicated pool with representative GPUs, run a synthetic workload and a replay of customer prompts to validate latency and cost per token. I'll put together a bench plan with the metrics: 95p latency, mean latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, token cost.
[00:05:04] Rina: Commercially, how do partners list on your marketplace? Is there revenue share or referral?
[00:05:11] Lena: That's more of a biz-dev discussion but we do have a partner program and marketplace listings; we can loop in the partnerships team. For this call we'll focus technical fit.
[00:05:20] Rina: OK. One thing from our engineering side — we use an annotation-based routing policy in the marketplace to route requests to partner endpoints, so the API surface needs to be consistent.
[00:05:31] Marcus: Redwood's API is REST + SDKs and has model cataloging + versioning. We also support structured outputs and tool-calling but for marketplace integration the key is stable endpoints, auth tokens, and usage metering. Billing can be per-token or via reserved capacity.
[00:05:49] Devon: How do you handle graceful degradation? If your hosted cluster is saturated, does traffic fail?
[00:05:54] Marcus: We have fallbacks to compatible model variants or other regions. Smart routing can steer traffic to dedicated capacity or a cheaper variant. For critical flows we'd recommend Dedicated or Private so you avoid noisy neighbor issues.
[00:06:08] Anika: Any tricky parts you see for integrating with Pelican?
[00:06:11] Marcus: Two things: 1) audit/log export formatting so it plugs into your SIEM, and 2) marketplace onboarding flow for SSO/SCIM and tenant isolation. Both are solvable but we'll need specifics from Devon/Mateo.
[00:06:26] Devon: We can provide the SIEM schema and SCIM endpoints.
[00:06:29] Lena: Great. We'll follow up with a small packet: partner integration checklist, security one-pager, and a pilot proposal.
[00:06:37] Rina: Sounds good. Also we'd like a short tech writeup for our marketplace docs so we can explain how Redwood partners will appear.
[00:06:44] Lena: We'll add that to the packet.
[00:06:47] Marcus: Quick note — some of the words in the auto transcription might be off. When we talk about KV cache we mean model key-value cache used to store past tokens for faster decode.
[00:06:58] Devon: Understood.
[00:07:00] [Silence for 12s] 
[00:07:12] Marcus: Questions from anyone?
[00:07:15] Rina: Not right now. Mate0, anything? (small laugh, mis-transcribed name)
[00:07:20] Mateo: Just that we'll need the SOC2 report before we go into a pilot with regulated partners.
[00:07:25] Lena: We'll share the SOC2 summary and can arrange an NDA if needed.
[00:07:30] [00:25:00] Marcus: (jump ahead in call) I wanted to sketch a minimal pilot: 1) 2-week perf run using a dedicated pool of 2 A100s; 2) replay of 100k example prompts from Pelican; 3) measure 95p latency and token cost; 4) walk-through integration points for SSO and audit logs. Would that fit your timeline?
[00:25:18] Devon: That sounds right. We were hoping to start a pilot in the next 2-4 weeks, so this aligns.
[00:25:23] Rina: From a BD perspective, if the pilot looks good we can discuss a co-marketing listing in the marketplace and a preferred partner designation.
[00:25:31] Lena: Great — we'll try to move quick. Marcus will own the tech plan.
[00:25:36] Marcus: I'll draft the bench plan and pilot checklist and share it in a doc. Also need the infra export from Devon.
[00:25:44] Devon: I'll pull that together.
[00:25:47] Anika: Any blockers on the Redwood side for privacy-preserving telemetry? We need to ensure no customer PII leaves our environment.
[00:25:55] Marcus: For hosted flows we can turn off application-level logging and only emit aggregated metrics. For private deployments you own the logs. We'll map exact fields to ensure nothing sensitive is shipped.
[00:26:07] Mateo: We'll need a short checklist for what you store and for how long.
[00:26:11] Lena: We'll include retention defaults and options in the security doc.
[00:26:16] [00:40:00] Rina: OK super. Last thing — can you include the rough commercial model in the partner packet? Just ballpark e.g., reserved monthly costs vs per-token.
[00:40:10] Lena: Yes, we'll include ballpark pricing and an example cost calc.
[00:40:18] Marcus: Anything else?
[00:40:21] Devon: No, that's it.
[00:40:23] Lena: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and set the technical deep-dive for next week.
[00:40:30] Rina: Thanks. Bye.
[00:40:33] [call ends]
